9861cf62476c90ae.name: Framework Audit and Maturation
9861cf62476c90ae.purpose: Fully audit the SYNTH framework, assess maturity and usability, identify gaps, and gather evidence for future cleanup and optimization missions.

4ab7e9d2cc7b1b66.name: Framework Maturation v2
4ab7e9d2cc7b1b66.purpose: Implement fixes for CLI next-command bugs, simplify expedition lifecycle, and optimize bootstrap performance based on the audit evaluation.

b536ecc7ceb9217a.name: Derived-State Integrity
b536ecc7ceb9217a.purpose: Eliminate the class of defects in which SYNTH's own read paths dirty the working tree, block expedition completion, or leave governance state uncommitted - by classifying every artifact once (durable, input, derived, cache, legacy) and enforcing two invariants: reads never write, and derived state never blocks work.

a57585f0aec4b2d8.name: Governed Operation from Operator Branches
a57585f0aec4b2d8.purpose: Make SYNTH govern work on pre-existing operator branches: declare and bind execution branches (ADR-056 --branch/--no-create), anchor and single-write the ceremony ledger (ADR-055: ledger writer, anchor, single writer), and make delivery and abandonment first-class ceremonies (deliver/seal/close/abandon) so finished work, files and history survive the branch lifecycle instead of being stranded or wiped.

b6ff1be26d13a677.name: Verification Coverage Truthfulness
b6ff1be26d13a677.purpose: Make SYNTH verification truthful: govern must execute the canonical registered test chain or fail loudly; remaining legacy event-log readers must migrate to event-stream; stale unregistered tests and evidence-manifest semantics must be resolved; and the expedition auto-commit convergence helper must complete so failures cannot remain hidden.

d0a701df55ef36d7.name: Initialize Audit and Evidence Gathering
d0a701df55ef36d7.goal: Audit the codebase, identify architectural gaps, evaluate usability, and propose follow-up expeditions based on findings.

3919441f53c3f36c.goal: Fix the bug where next command suggestions reference incorrect Mission/Expedition IDs when creating or managing drafts to improve robustness and ease of use.
3919441f53c3f36c.forceReason: Working directory contains temporary audit reports and scratch files.

dac069e8cc375a6b.forceReason: PR #302 full-govern green; dirty tree is only derived artifacts (certification-matrix.md, proof/*) which are intentionally not committed per derived-file policy. Expedition work (Simplify Expedition Lifecycle Operations) is merged-ready.

ceaa59bf74771ca0.name: Optimize CLI Bootstrap Performance
ceaa59bf74771ca0.goal: Profile and optimize the 13-step infrastructure bootstrap and event replay to reduce CLI command latency.
ceaa59bf74771ca0.forceReason: Working directory contains temporary audit reports and scratch files.

247c03330b22eee0.name: Dead Code Elimination (Exports)
247c03330b22eee0.goal: Remove unused exported functions and types across the framework to reduce the API surface and overall codebase size.

d7abae63e9eedf10.goal: Refactor and simplify the internal dependency graph to prevent circular dependencies and improve maintainability.
d7abae63e9eedf10.forceReason: Working directory contains temporary audit reports and scratch files.

3ea6dbc99dd69a09.name: Address Monolithic State Files in .synth/data/
3ea6dbc99dd69a09.goal: Analyze and implement a strategy (such as event log rotation, compaction, or state partitioning) to prevent state files from growing indefinitely and creating performance bottlenecks.

4a3f7b93a4cc3e53.name: Validation Assertion Quiet Output Flag
4a3f7b93a4cc3e53.goal: Add a flag/option to the validation engine and CLI to suppress passing test details and only output errors or failing tests, reducing console output saturation.

912a468ae9bf5bd6.name: Remove Legacy Support for Previous Synth Projects
912a468ae9bf5bd6.goal: Deprecate and remove backwards-compatibility layers and migrations designed for legacy Synth v1 projects, simplifying codebase maintenance since there are no active legacy installations in the wild.

0bd85610bca114c9.name: Investigate 13 Event System Bureaucracy
0bd85610bca114c9.goal: Investigate and propose strategies to alleviate the bureaucracy of the 13-event system in Synth development

c6f9251b64466f29.name: Human-Readable Expedition Branch Naming
c6f9251b64466f29.goal: Replace cryptic raw-ID branch names with slug-based names (expedition/<mission-slug>/<expedition-slug>-<expId[0:7]>) while preserving determinism, uniqueness, and traceability so checkpoint and branch-policy enforcement still resolve correctly.

190a72e71fbe3c14.name: Single-Source Branch Naming
190a72e71fbe3c14.goal: Move branch-name composition out of branch-creation methods into mission/expedition composition; resolve names through a single source of truth; remove redundant legacy/candidate helpers if unneeded; align checkpoint types.

5c2b2db11e77e740.name: Fix --dry-run persisting state mutations
5c2b2db11e77e740.goal: Investigate and fix the --dry-run flag in mutating CLI subcommands (expedition create, delete) so it never persists draft files, canonical-state, or event-log entries. Reproducer: two consecutive dry-run and real expedition-create invocations both logged EXPEDITION_CREATED events and persisted draft files (fdc1558fa0a676d7 was an accidental dry-run survivor). Dry-run must be read-only; observability of the intended mutation must come from preview output only.

d8a555db237507e5.name: Harden draft lifecycle integrity
d8a555db237507e5.goal: Prove that draft creation/deletion is atomic, chain-safe, and approved without manual file surgery: (1) never manually rm/edit .synth/data/drafts/ files; all removal via CLI. (2) 'expedition delete' cleans up draft json+integrity files in the same transaction as the state mutation. (3) Fix --dry-run create bug that leaked draft file writes to disk. (4) Approved drafts are committed to the execution gate immediately rather than left as loose drafts.

metadata.refinementNote: Deliverables implemented: dry-run create no longer persists; delete and commit retire draft artifacts chain-safely (retireDraftArtifacts GC). Also raised reuse-and-templates spawn timeout 60s->240s: bootstrap takes ~44s on this machine, 3/3 false failures at 60s pre-change.

20d934325ee30c1a.name: Resolve ExecutionGate legacy-only branch enforcement
20d934325ee30c1a.goal: Prove that execution branch enforcement accepts every canonical branch form the CLI generates: the EXECUTION_BRANCH_CHECK phase computes candidates without mission/expedition names and demands only the legacy raw-ID form (expedition/<missionId>/<expeditionId>), while ensureExpeditionBranch and assertExecutionBranch accept the preferred slug form — so starting any expedition on its slug-form branch is rejected by the gate that the CLI itself satisfied. Enrich the gate check with names from canonical state so both layers resolve identical candidate sets; cover with tests/execution-branch-gate.test.js

4b5694ab06ccb652.name: Debranch expedition completion
4b5694ab06ccb652.goal: Prove that concluding an expedition never requires its canonical branch to exist: CompleteExpedition leaves the branch-gated set (only StartExpedition remains gated, since its branch exists by construction at start time) because a completion-time branch may already be merged and deleted, may never have existed, or may be unavailable on another checkout. Align the CLI guard, ExecutionGate phase, and checkpoint step; update tests/execution-branch-gate.test.js

bc9c51e0674ec0ef.name: Unify expedition and mission termination commands
bc9c51e0674ec0ef.goal: DELIVERY ITEM: a concise termination model for expeditions and missions — clear, simple, leaving no room for pollution artifacts. Today the conclusion surface is scattered across complete, finish, archive, cancel (and archive doubles as cleanup fallback), each with different gates, evidence rules, and artifact side-effects; users cannot predict which command leaves which state behind. Collapse the surface into a minimal explicit model: few conclusion verbs with deterministic preconditions, exactly one event trail per termination path, and mandatory retirement of derived artifacts (drafts, loose files) in the same transition so terminal states never leave pollution behind

3c84f699a7c932fc.name: Investigate cross-branch event-log linearity during expedition closure
3c84f699a7c932fc.goal: Formalize the fast-forward-before-finish closure pattern proven live on d8a555db237507e5 and 20d934325ee30c1a: finishing on a canonical branch whose tip is a strict ancestor of main kept the derived event log linear across three branches and avoided replay divergence on later merges. Investigate (1) when lifecycle-event-bearing branches diverge from main and what replay and merge hazards follow, including interaction with existing repair tooling, (2) whether fast-forward reconciliation is always safe and how to detect mechanically when it is not, (3) what the CLI owes operators here: pre-finish ancestry verification, warnings, or automatic reconciliation. Deliverable: evidence-based findings plus zero or more follow-up expedition proposals for automation or documentation

e617ccd0ac6d60b8.name: Verify event-log lineage before lifecycle mutations
e617ccd0ac6d60b8.goal: Guard every lifecycle mutation (expedition approve, commit, start, finish, complete, archive, cancel) against forking the derived event log across branches: before mutating, compare the current branch's .synth/data/event-log.jsonl against the richest known log among local refs and origin/main; accept when it is a strict prefix (stale-but-safe, matching the proven fast-forward-before-finish protocol from investigation 3c84f699a7c932fc), block or warn when other refs carry exclusive events the current log lacks, and print reconciliation guidance (fast-forward when ancestor, explicit merge order otherwise). Implement in the CLI pre-flight layer, not inside the ExecutionGate, which stays untouched

71ce984c9d3dd48f.name: Introduce DRY and SDK compliance certification into the expedition lifecycle
71ce984c9d3dd48f.goal: Add a compliance check to the expedition lifecycle that statically inspects an expedition's deliverables for DRY violations and SDK-state-mutation misuse, and emits a machine-readable certification attached as expedition evidence. The certification is either CERTIFIED (full DRY + SDK evidence) or NOT_REQ (explicit, valid reasons the checks do not apply, e.g. no source deliverables or only derived/doc files). The check must run non-mutating: it adds NO extra lifecycle events beyond the evidence attachment.

70a5c5ed2bda5f1b.name: Audit CLI command surface and decouple synth.js
70a5c5ed2bda5f1b.goal: INVESTIGATION. Survey every CLI verb/subcommand (mission, expedition, evidence, validate, explain, docs, bootstrap, etc.) and quantify redundancy: overlapping procedures that can collapse into a smaller, memorable command set, reducing the operator 'knowledge quorum'. Map findings against existing related expeditions so the audit extends rather than duplicates them: bc9c51e0 (termination-model unification), dac069e8 (lifecycle simplification), ceaa59bf (bootstrap-performance). Identify where synth.js loads the full machinery (13-step bootstrap, all adapters, Mission Studio, Planning Cognition) on every invocation, and propose decoupling: lazy/deferred per-command loading, command-group entry points, and a thinner default path. Deliverable: a written audit plus follow-up expedition drafts minted from concrete findings (e.g. verb consolidation, lazy CLI loader).

e5fdf75656be46bb.name: Decouple synth.js: lazy-load command groups and thin CLI entrypoint
e5fdf75656be46bb.goal: Refactor src/cli/synth.ts so the top-level entrypoint performs only argument parsing + dispatch. Each command group (expedition, mission, program, explain, verify, docs, etc.) is loaded lazily on first invocation; the 13-step bootstrap, all adapters, Mission Studio, and Planning Cognition are imported only by commands that need them. Measurable target: cold-start of 'synth version' / 'synth status' must not load adapters or Mission Studio. Deliverable: lazy loader + per-group entrypoints + a cold-start benchmark.

metadata.refinementNote: FINAL DESIGN: thin entrypoint parses argv[2] then dynamic import('./groups/<group>.js'); Mission Studio/Planning Cognition/adapters load only inside the group that needs them. Command-weight gate: light groups (version/help/status/explain/docs) SKIP the 13-step bootstrap; heavy groups run it inside their module. Benchmark: version/help <100ms, status/explain <300ms cold. Implement BEFORE verb consolidation (restructures dispatch first).
metadata.cancelReason: Precursor to 68b59f0e6029b7ac (verb-consolidation). Implementing now would re-touch src/cli/synth.ts already modified by merged 68b59f0e (commit 80a93b4) and duplicate approved lazy-load expeditions 97ddb728c5250c96 + ff268079bb596ef3. Closing to avoid side effects/regressions.

68b59f0e6029b7ac.name: Consolidate CLI verbs into a minimal, memorable command set
68b59f0e6029b7ac.goal: Propose and implement a reduced command vocabulary that collapses redundant verbs while preserving capability. Coordinate with bc9c51e0 (termination unification): adopt a single lifecycle create->approve->start->finish with --disposition for expedition/mission; unify validate/verify/govern into 'check' (--dry-run|--full, --repair); unify status/checkpoint/explain status/report into 'status'; unify init/bootstrap/genesis/discover/migrate into 'init'. Deliverable: command-map migration plan + deprecated-alias shims + docs update.

metadata.refinementNote: FINAL DESIGN: one shared verb vocabulary across mission+expedition (create->approve->start->finish --disposition complete|archive|cancel; evidence/show/list/report/move/delete explicit). check=validate; check --full absorbs validate --full + verify(no-sub) + govern validation; check --repair=repair. govern=release gate (build+test+audit+proof). verify=signatures only. status absorbs checkpoint; explain=deep; init/--import absorbs discover+migrate. doctor absorbs support verbs. Implement AFTER loader lands.

ff268079bb596ef3.name: CLI Lazy-Load Strategy
ff268079bb596ef3.goal: Map the current synth.js bootstrap cost, identify command-group lazy boundaries, design the per-command-group lazy-loading model (shared bootstrap vs deferred domain graph), and define benchmarks and acceptance criteria so light commands stay bootstrap-free and heavy commands load only their group.

97ddb728c5250c96.name: Migrate synth.js to Lazy-Load Model
97ddb728c5250c96.goal: Migrate the monolithic synth.js heavy-load path to the per-command-group lazy-loading model defined by the CLI Lazy-Load Strategy expedition, preserving byte-identical command output and keeping light commands (version, help, status, explain replay/identity/resume/governance) bootstrap-free.

f4e4850f5929a111.name: Audit expedition model: dependsOn enforcement and keep/remove decision
f4e4850f5929a111.goal: Determine whether the expedition model enforces the dependsOn property. Current evidence: checkUpstreamDependencies (lifecycle-completion based) is advisory-only (reported as a warning in expedition check/doctor), while isBlockedByUpstreamGate (review-gate based) blocks execution in domain/execution.ts and governance/intake.ts. Decide which dependency mechanisms to keep, harden (e.g., enforce lifecycle completion at start), or remove, and recommend the target model.

beb71bb77cb510e3.name: Canonicalize and standardize logs
beb71bb77cb510e3.goal: Establish one canonical logging model for SYNTH: consolidate CLI error logs (cli-errors.jsonl), runtime diagnostics, event logs, and proof/temp artifacts into a single location, consistent schema, and rotation policy. Eliminate ad-hoc/duplicate logs (e.g., cli-errors.jsonl vs a referenced cli-errors.log, per-test temp logs under /var/folders) and standardize structured stdout vs diagnostic streams so operators and tooling depend on one shape.

4ce3c7bcef3a00d5.name: Event schema versioning and migration registry
4ce3c7bcef3a00d5.goal: Add schemaVersion to every event and a MigrationRegistry so replay survives event-shape evolution; version canonical-state by schema.

29b9a3704eb1287c.name: Fold legacy CLI verbs into the canonical command set
29b9a3704eb1287c.goal: Consolidate redundant verbs via deprecated-alias shims and a unified 'init' entrypoint, preserving first-contact/genesis/bootstrap/discover/governance subsystems and their tests. Canonical targets: status (was report/explain status), validate verify (was verify), docs agents (was project AGENTS.md), init --brownfield/--analyze/--greenfield (was bootstrap/discover/first-contact/genesis). Deprecate intent + migrate as load-bearing-for-alignment legacy verbs.

729e4e2c17add703.name: Allow archiving completed expeditions
729e4e2c17add703.goal: The 'expedition archive' lifecycle rule is inverted: it rejects archiving a COMPLETED expedition ('Only active or paused expeditions can be archived') while archiving is conceptually for finished/superseded work. Fix so a completed expedition can be archived (e.g., to retire a superseded duplicate). Scope: (1) intake.ts expedition.archive gate — add 'completed' to allowed source statuses (keep 'cancelled'/'archived' terminal, keep 'active'/'paused' allowed); (2) domain/planning.ts archiveExpedition — remove the 'cannot archive a completed expedition' invariant; (3) update the lifecycle comment at intake.ts:10-11; (4) add a regression test. Consider whether a dedicated 'superseded' disposition is cleaner than completed->archived and recommend in the plan.

0463c2cae71ac727.name: Pointer-based evidence and derived-artifact exclusion from completion gate
0463c2cae71ac727.goal: Reduce SYNTH's content redundancy and the commit-then-complete friction by (1) making evidence pointer-based: event-log/evidence records reference external artifacts by git SHA / content hash / URL instead of embedding content copies or full git diffs; completion records 'gitHead' as the realized-state pointer; (2) excluding derived/generated paths (proof/, dist/, *.integrity.json, canonical-state.json) from the DirtyWorkingTreeBlocksCompletion gate so only uncommitted IN-SCOPE SOURCE blocks completion; (3) keeping the event log as the authoritative provenance ledger while git remains the content store. Scope: locate the completion dirty-tree enforcement (cmdExpeditionComplete / CompleteExpedition capability) and the evidence-attach path; add a derived-path allowlist; record gitHead on EXPEDITION_COMPLETED. Preserve replay independence by keeping event-log.jsonl as the durable core. Add tests. Consider a short ADR noting the provenance-vs-content split.

761c9be33f165253.name: Stage 0: Audit governance-cluster verbs & blast radius
761c9be33f165253.goal: Map governance-cluster verbs (validate, verify, govern, checkpoint, approval, certify): every CLI invocation site, CI/script references (npm run govern), documentation mentions, and operator muscle-memory dependencies. Produce a blast-radius report identifying which renames break CI vs which are safe. Read-only research; no source changes.

Produce an ADR with chosen model, rationale, and affected command/CI/doc graph. No source changes.

424e13e73c362f3b.name: Stage 2: Implement safe governance folds (verify->validate verify, checkpoint->status)
424e13e73c362f3b.goal: Low-risk deprecated-alias shims: verify->validate verify, checkpoint->status (pre-flight as a status mode). Add emitDeprecation notices, command-safety classification, help text. Keep govern/validate/approval/certify canonical. Build + verify.

17a5c207277389ae.name: Stage 3: Migrate CI/docs/scripts for any govern rename (gated, optional)

eb5e0740225fdb11.name: Stage 4: Verify govern-evolution (full pipeline + replay)
eb5e0740225fdb11.goal: After governance-cluster changes, run full govern pipeline and confirm replay consistency (synth explain replay) with no CI regression and operator flows intact.

0daac4fc9df96606.name: Fix mission.approve gate scoping (checks active mission instead of target mission)
0daac4fc9df96606.goal: intake.ts mission.approve resolves missionId = action.missionId || activeMission?.id; CLI passes no missionId, so it inspects the ACTIVE mission's executing expeditions, wrongly blocking approval of an UNRELATED mission. Fix: resolve the target mission from the approved draft/snapshot and check THAT mission for executing expeditions, so a mission with no executing expeditions can be approved even when another mission has a live expedition. See attached finding.

3d9f5d0df805e15f.name: Implement mission new / expedition new commands (replace over-complicated mission create)
3d9f5d0df805e15f.goal: Replace the draft-proposal mission create flow with a single canonicalizing 'mission new' (and 'expedition new') command, per the verb-consolidation plan. The new command should canonicalize a draft mission (emit MISSION_CREATED draft) so expeditions can be planned immediately, subsuming the 'mission create canonicalize draft' structural fix. See attached evidence.

e8ba8f92d0105412.name: Fix derived-state auto-commit (EXP-AUTO-COMMIT-001) to skip gitignored paths
e8ba8f92d0105412.goal: autoCommitDerivedState (src/cli/synth.ts ~351) builds an explicit git add path list that includes .synth/data/drafts/ (gitignored), causing the whole git add to error and the derived-state commit to abort, leaving event-log.jsonl/canonical-state.json staged-but-uncommitted after lifecycle transitions. Fix: exclude gitignored/derived-excluded paths before git add (filter via git check-ignore, or use git add -A which skips ignored). See attached finding.

metadata.cancelReason: Premise no longer holds: .synth/data/drafts/ is tracked, not gitignored (git check-ignore exits 1), and completed expedition ecc3688796be0545 'Derived-state staging correctness (auto-commit + ignore filtering)' delivered the ignore-filtering fix. Ceremony commits now stage draft files successfully, so the EXP-AUTO-COMMIT-001 failure mode is gone.

1ad8b22eace9855a.name: Make expedition charters the primary enforced dependency source
1ad8b22eace9855a.goal: Make docs/expeditions/<id>.md charter **Depends On:** / **Blocks:** the single source of truth for expedition dependencies, eliminating the need for a --depends-on flag. (1) Ensure target 4ab7e9d2 expeditions have charters (generate if missing). (2) Make isBlockedByUpstreamGate (intake.ts:233, execution.ts:325) charter-aware so declared dependencies block downstream CLI commands/intents. (3) Wire the linear sequence by editing each charter Depends On to reference the previous expedition. Lifecycle (change/remove/reparent/edit) is a charter edit only - no dual source, no flag soup.

31a26dadaf47a42d.name: Adapter configuration consolidated: declared vs detected
31a26dadaf47a42d.goal: Adapter configuration has no home. It is spread across five places with no authority order and no schema. (a) .synth/config.yaml holds a single `git:` block, parsed ad hoc by three independent modules (ledger/branch.ts:74, adapter/git-snapshot.ts:338, repository/branch-policy.ts) with no type, no loader module and no validation, so an unknown or misspelled key is silently ignored. (b) `synth init` writes detection results into the generated manifest under `adapters: {selected, config, diagnostics}` (cli/synth.ts:3070-3090) - a regenerable document, and absent from this repository manifest altogether. (c) .synth/context.json persists a repository classification (`repositoryType: brownfield-polyglot`, confidence, derivedFrom) but no adapter configuration. (d) `synth adapter configure repository path=. remote=origin defaultBranch=main promotionMode=direct` (cli/adapter.ts:11,74-86) is accepted and then lost: GitRepositoryAdapter.configure (adapters/repository/git.ts:187-199) merges into in-memory state and never writes, so the verb has no durable effect across a process restart. (e) Forge credentials are split between env GITHUB_TOKEN and a config schema that declares `token` required (adapters/github/adapter.ts:72), which invites a personal access token into tracked YAML. The consequence is measured, not theoretical: detectRecommendedAdapters already computes defaultBranch and remote (cli/detect-adapters.ts:113-119) and both are dropped, so the same fact is hardcoded three separate times (ledger/delivery.ts:347 defaults baseBranches to ["origin/main","main"] and no caller ever passes the option; ledger/branch.ts:49 LEDGER_FALLBACK_BRANCH = "main"; cli/adapter.ts:81 defaultBranch || "main"). Outcome required: (1) a typed `adapters:` section in .synth/config.yaml - adapters.repository.{provider,remote,baseBranch,snapshots,hooks} and adapters.forge.{provider,owner,repo,baseUrl} - read through one new loader module with schema validation that warns on unknown keys. (2) Detected observations written to .synth/cache/adapters.json (gitignored, artifact class `cache` per state/artifact-policy.ts:58, same precedent as dependency-records.json), each carrying value, confidence and derivedFrom, and including a git BINARY probe so that "git is not installed" is distinguishable from "git is installed but this directory is not a repository". Today first-contact onboard:detect returns byte-identical output for both cases and advises `synth adapter init` even when git is absent, which is advice the operator cannot follow. (3) A documented and tested authority order: CLI flag, then config.yaml, then cached detection, then built-in default - where the built-in default is provider none declaring no capabilities, never origin/main. (4) The three hardcoded branch defaults deleted and fed from configuration through the baseBranches option ledger/delivery.ts:347 already accepts. (5) `synth adapter configure --approve` promotes a detection proposal into config.yaml, plan-then-approve in the same shape as first-contact onboard --approve; this single mechanism is what makes the greenfield offer ("git is installed, this is not a repository - initialise it?") and the brownfield offer ("a repository and a GitHub remote were detected - configure the forge adapter?") the same code path. (6) Credentials resolved from env or a secret store only, with `token` removed from the GitHub adapter required config schema. (7) The existing `git:` block migrated to adapters.repository.* with a deprecation warning on read, and `git.ledgerBranch` retired: the ledger branch is inferred from the checkout when it matches branchPolicy.declaredPatterns, with trunk as the last resort rather than the first. (8) The ledger-branch fallback order corrected - a stale configured value plus a stale .synth/data/ledger.json record (currently arena/c5db653e-synth) resolve to local `main` today, which would commit governance state onto the trunk branch instead of the declared operator checkout; a checkout matching a declared pattern must win over trunk. Acceptance: the three-system matrix (no git at all / git installed without a repository / git installed with a repository) yields distinct, truthful recognition output and identical ledger behaviour in all three; no repository or branch value is hardcoded outside the loader documented defaults; `synth adapter configure` survives a process restart; no secret can be written into .synth/config.yaml; and the ledger records ceremonies with zero VCS present, reporting verification as unavailable rather than failing.

2c9c6c62a727ece8.name: Verification sees the whole event log
2c9c6c62a727ece8.goal: The framework integrity evidence is vacuous on any repository whose event log has been chunked. src/verification/context.ts:44,62 computes `hasEventLog = migratedEvents.length > 0 || await pathExists(eventLogPath)` where eventLogPath is sdk.paths.eventLogFile(root) - the legacy single file .synth/data/event-log.jsonl. This repository log lives at .synth/data/event-stream/partition-<n>/segment-XXXX.jsonl (four partitions, 442 events), the layout documented at src/runtime/governance-resolver.ts:84 and read by SegmentStore (src/infra/event-store.ts:325). So hasEventLog is false, and in order: verification/checks.ts:44 returns ReplayIntegrity "pass" with the message "No event log present; replay integrity is vacuously satisfied"; checks.ts:117 and checks.ts:386 skip their event-log-gated assertions; verification/engine.ts:29 skips replay entirely; and cli/synth.ts:862-869 (verifyReplayHealth) reports "No event log present; replay skipped" inside `synth checkpoint`. At the same moment `synth explain replay` reads the partitioned store correctly and reports 442 events, consistent, chain valid. The two disagree and the disagreement is invisible: the check whose only job is proving the ledger is intact reports success without ever looking at it. Every green validate, govern and full-govern run on a chunked repository - including the one that certified PR #343 - carried that vacuous pass. The same legacy-path assumption is spread across at least seven further call sites: cli/bootstrap-apply.ts:235, cli/explain-observability.ts:110, cli/explain-paths.ts:57, cli/explain-replay-light.ts:49, cli/first-contact.ts:746, 780 and 826. Two complications make this more than a one-line fix. First, THREE layouts coexist in the codebase: the legacy single file, event-stream/partition-<n>.jsonl (still implemented by PartitionStore.filePath at event-store.ts:161-162) and the current event-stream/partition-<n>/segment-XXXX.jsonl - so the codebase carries two contradictory ideas of what a partition is. Second, the vocabulary cannot express the truth: verification/types.ts:14 declares `CheckStatus = "pass" | "fail" | "warn"` with no skipped value, which is precisely why an absent log is reported as a pass instead of as a non-result. Outcome required: (1) ONE authority for where the event log is and whether there is one - a single resolver recognising all three layouts and returning present, layout, paths and eventCount - consumed by verification/context, verifyReplayHealth and every call site listed above; after this, no module may construct or test the legacy path directly. (2) A vacuous pass becomes impossible: CheckStatus gains `skipped` carrying a structured reason (the same shape EXP-TEST-004 proposes for test skips), ReplayIntegrity reports skipped with reason no-event-log when there is genuinely no log, and reports the eventCount it actually replayed when there is one. (3) `synth checkpoint` replay step names the layout and the event count verified, and can never again print "No event log present" for a repository holding 442 events. (4) PartitionStore stale partition-<n>.jsonl naming is either reconciled with the segment layout or explicitly marked legacy-read-only, so two contradictory partition layouts stop shipping side by side. (5) Tests pin all three layouts: a segment-partitioned ledger must yield a ReplayIntegrity result naming its eventCount; a legacy single-file ledger must still verify; an empty project must report skipped rather than pass; and a regression guard must fail if any module reintroduces a direct legacy-path existence check. Acceptance: on this repository `synth checkpoint` and `synth validate` report replay over 442 events instead of skipping; ReplayIntegrity and `explain replay` agree; and no verification check is able to report pass without having read the log.

metadata.refinementNote: CORRECTION to the drafted goal, recorded during implementation as required by the append-only ledger. The goal asserted that verification/checks.ts:44 returns a vacuous ReplayIntegrity pass on this repository and that every green validate/govern/full-govern run carried it. That is FALSE and was measured wrong. buildVerificationContext (src/verification/context.ts:53-63) already builds the partition-aware store: createInfra returns a PartitionedEventStore, eventStore.loadAll() returns 448 events here, hasEventLog is true, and `synth verify` reports ReplayIntegrity pass with the message 'Chain valid, replay consistent, graph valid (448 events)'. All six checks pass on real evidence. What IS true, and is the defect this expedition fixes: (1) verifyReplayHealth (src/cli/synth.ts:862-869) tests only sdk.paths.eventLogFile(root) - the legacy single file - so `synth checkpoint` reports 'No event log present; replay skipped' for a ledger holding 448 events; (2) the same legacy-path-only assumption is served to operators and agents by explain paths, explain observability, explain replay-light, first-contact (746, 780, 826) and bootstrap-apply:235, none of which mention the event-stream layout that actually exists on disk; (3) a genuinely empty project still reports ReplayIntegrity as pass rather than as a non-result, because CheckStatus (verification/types.ts:14) has no skipped value; (4) three log layouts coexist with no single resolver. Scope narrows accordingly: the verification engine is NOT broken and must not be rewritten; the presence-and-location question is answered in seven places by one wrong path, and that is what gets unified.
